This market will resolve to "Yes" if both West Ham United FC and Everton FC each score at least one goal during the game.

This market will resolve to "No" if either team fails to score (i.e., if one or both teams finish with zero goals).

If the game is postponed, this market will remain open until the game has been completed. If the game is canceled entirely, with no make-up game, this market will resolve 50–50.

If the game is started but not completed, this market will resolve according to the official final score published on premierleague.com. This market refers only to the outcome within the first 90 minutes of regular play plus stoppage time.

The primary resolution source for this market is the official statistics of the event as recognized by the governing body or event organizers. However, if the governing body or event organizers have not published final match statistics within 2 hours after the event's conclusion, a consensus of credible reporting may be used instead.

eventMetadata.context_description: West Ham United host Everton in a crucial Premier League clash on April 25, with the Hammers sitting 17th on 32 points in relegation peril after a vital 4-0 win over Wolves last weekend climbed them out of the drop zone. That momentum contrasts their prior FA Cup penalty exit to Leeds, amid injury returns like Crysencio Summerville boosting squad depth despite lingering knocks to Fabianski and others. Everton, comfortably 8th on 47 points, arrive nearly fully fit following boosts for Jarrad Branthwaite, Iliman Ndiaye, and Vitalii Mykolenko, though Charly Alcaraz and Jack Grealish remain sidelined. West Ham's home form tempers Everton's superior head-to-head edge and table position, heightening stakes in the relegation scrap versus mid-table security.

eventMetadata.context_description: Tottenham Hotspur's official announcement two days ago appointing Roberto De Zerbi as new head coach on a five-year contract has driven trader consensus to 100% implied probability, following Igor Tudor's mutual departure after just seven games amid a desperate Premier League relegation fight. The Italian, fresh from stints at Brighton and Marseille, replaces a string of short-term managers this season, with Spurs one point above the drop zone and seven matches remaining. De Zerbi's attacking style aligns with fan expectations, though some supporters' groups protest his past comments. Realistic challenges include work permit delays or an unprecedented board reversal, but confirmation solidifies his position ahead of his debut versus Sunderland.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus favors Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes at 46.5% implied probability for PFA Players' Player of the Year, propelled by his league-leading 17 assists, 99 chances created, and 83 key passes through 29 matches, fueling United's third-place standing amid a tight title race. Aston Villa's Morgan Rogers follows at 31.1%, buoyed by his eight goals and standout rankings in Sky Sports' top 25 players, supporting Villa's fourth-place surge. Arsenal's Declan Rice, at 29.0%, anchors the table-topping Gunners' midfield with elite chance creation and power rankings dominance, as recent Sky Sports (March 20) and F365 analyses elevate both Fernandes and Rice following United and Arsenal's strong runs over the past month. Erling Haaland lags despite leading the Golden Boot race, reflecting City's second-place position and voter emphasis on all-around impact.

title: Will TheUnitedStrand get a haircut by 2025-26 season end?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Frank Ilett (theunitedstrand) gets a haircut after Manchester United has won five consecutive competitive games by May 24, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

For the purpose of this market, a draw or loss resets the consecutive win counter. Unbeaten streaks are not included. The haircut must occur after the fifth consecutive win has been completed.

A “haircut” refers to a clearly visible and noticeable shortening to his hair, small adjustments of an inch or two will not qualify unless they are a clear result of a haircut. 

Taking a little snip or minor trim on stream (or in a video) also does not count. It must be a real, substantial haircut that noticeably changes his appearance from the long hair style he's maintained.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Bruno Fernandes commands 97.9% implied probability as Premier League most assists leader, reflecting his insurmountable 17-assist tally through 29 matches—seven clear of Rayan Cherki's 10 for Manchester City—bolstered by recent record-breaking feats like surpassing David Beckham's Manchester United single-season mark and his March Player of the Month award. Consistent creativity from the Red Devils captain, including key chances created in a recent loss to Leeds, has widened the gap amid fewer than 10 fixtures remaining, with United facing Chelsea and Brentford next. Challengers like Cherki (facing Arsenal then Burnley), Granit Xhaka, Mohammed Kudus, and Jack Grealish would need extraordinary hauls—coupled with Fernandes injury, suspension, or load management—to close the deficit realistically.

eventMetadata.context_description: David Raya's commanding 88.4% implied probability stems from his lead with 15 clean sheets in 32 Premier League appearances, three clear of Manchester City's Gianluigi Donnarumma and four ahead of Everton's Jordan Pickford, bolstered by Arsenal's league-best defensive record of just 29 goals conceded amid their title-chasing form (21 wins, 7 draws, 4 losses). Recent matchday results solidified his edge, with Arsenal securing another shutout while challengers faltered slightly. Trader consensus prices in Arsenal's favorable run-in against mid-table sides like Bournemouth and Burnley. Realistic challenges include a Raya injury, Arsenal defensive lapses in high-stakes clashes like the April 19 Manchester City trip, or flawless clean-sheet streaks by Donnarumma or Pickford in their tighter schedules.

title: Will any Premier League club reach 90 points?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if any English Premier League (EPL) reaches at least 90 points in the 2025-26 Premier League season. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source will be official information from the English Premier League (https://www.premierleague.com/en/tables).

eventMetadata.context_description: Arsenal lead the Premier League table on 70 points after 32 matches, with just six games remaining—yielding a maximum of 88 points and rendering 90 unattainable for any club. This mathematical certainty drives 100% trader consensus on "No," solidified by Arsenal's 1-2 loss to Bournemouth on April 11, which squandered vital late points in the title race. Manchester City trail on 61 points from 30 games (max 85), while Manchester United (55, max 76) and Aston Villa (54, max 75) are even farther adrift. Despite tight Champions League spots for the top five, remaining fixtures, fatigue from European commitments, and inconsistent form eliminate upset paths to 90 points.

title: Will any of the Big Six EPL clubs miss European football?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if at least one of the following clubs — Arsenal, Chelsea, Liverpool, Manchester City, Manchester United, or Tottenham Hotspur — fails to qualify for any European (UEFA) football competition (UEFA Champions League, UEFA Europa League, or UEFA Conference League) for the 2026-2027 European season. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A club will be considered to have qualified for a UEFA competition if it earns entry into any stage of that competition for the 2026–27 season, including any qualifying round or play-off round. Qualification includes qualifying for any of the 2026-2027 UEFA competitions by winning a 2025-2026 UEFA competition.

If European qualification is not officially finalized by July 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve based on the official determinations available at that time. If at least one of the clubs has not officially qualified for one of the three competitions by July 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Yes".

The primary resolution source will be official information from UEFA; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus heavily favors Michael Carrick at 53.5% implied probability to become Manchester United's next permanent head coach, driven by his strong interim performance since replacing Ruben Amorim in January 2026, with recent form improvements and unbeaten runs bolstering his case amid a thorough club review. Pundits like Gary Neville and Roy Keane debated his permanency just yesterday, highlighting Old Trafford pressure-handling and no formal outreach to rivals yet as of early April. Oliver Glasner (7.5%) edges ahead on availability post-Crystal Palace links, while Luis Enrique (5.9%) and Thomas Tuchel (5.2%) linger as high-profile options with Premier League appeal, though Carrick's internal momentum and collaborative model fit dominate sentiment ahead of a pre-World Cup decision.

eventMetadata.context_description: Rayan Cherki's 10 Premier League assists in Manchester City's 2025/26 title-chasing campaign trail the single-season record of 20 shared by Thierry Henry and Kevin De Bruyne by a wide margin, with roughly six matches left before the May finale. Trader consensus at 99.2% "No" stems from his sustainable pace—averaging under 0.4 assists per game despite 1,384 minutes played—making the required 1.7-per-game surge mathematically improbable amid competition from Haaland, Foden, and Doku for service opportunities. Recent highlights include Pep Guardiola's praise after a 3-0 Chelsea win, where Cherki shone, but no injury windfalls or rotation shifts elevate odds. Only an unprecedented hot streak or mass absences could theoretically shift this, though historical precedents are absent.
